name: Industrial Products
meaning: Heavily sold; no broad rebound yet
summary: Industrial Products stocks have been sold broadly. In the last 30 sessions the share above their 50-day average fell as low as 8%, and today it is 24%. The equal-weighted Industrial Products index is 9.6% below its 52-week high. A thrust (the share above the 9-day average jumping from 20% or less to 80% or more within 5 sessions) is what the rules look for next. None has followed yet.
rule: At some point in the last 30 sessions, fewer than 40% of the stocks were above their 50-day average.

study.state: Every thrust in the study came out of a washout, but washouts often lasted weeks before one came (industries spent 13% of all days in Washout). On its own a washout says nothing about timing.
study.market: Market context mattered more than the thrust type. Thrusts while the Nifty 50 was below its 200-day average were followed by +6.5 points over 60 sessions even without 2020 (62% rose 15% first; 215 cases in 36 weeks); thrusts while it was above, by -2.2 points. This split was examined after seeing the results, and 36 separate weeks is a small sample.
study.rallies: Of 285 big rallies (an industry index rising 25% or more within 120 sessions of a 60-session low), a C or CAP thrust came within 20 sessions of the low in 145 (51%), typically 5 sessions after it.
study.leader_flag: Full flags (industry 15% or more below its high): in 644 cases the stock did 6.0% better than its industry over the next 120 sessions on average (median +2.8%; 55% beat it), while an average stock of the same industry on the same days did -0.2% (43% beat it). In 2020 flagged stocks did 3.9% worse. The softer 10-15% tier showed no difference (+0.8% average, median -1.5%; 837 cases).
study.quarter: At a C thrust, the top quarter by 6-month return did 0.8 points better than its industry over the next 60 sessions and the bottom quarter 1.6 points worse; the median stock in every quarter trailed the equal-weighted industry index. After a CAP thrust there was no clear order.
study.bottom: No meaningful difference: at thrusts, stocks that bottomed before their industry and were above their 20-day average did 0.2 points better than their industry over 60 sessions; the others 0.3-0.6 points worse.
study.limits: NSE daily data from Jan 2016; cases from Jan 2017 to Oct 2026 across 46 NSE industry and sector groups. The stock list is rebuilt every month from what was known then, including companies later delisted. Limits: industries often signal in the same weeks, so cases are not independent; the leader-flag and capitulation cut-offs come from the earlier study, and the market-context split was examined after seeing results; NSE's industry labels are today's; trading costs are ignored.

market.note: The Nifty 50 is below its 200-day average. In the study, industry thrusts in such markets were followed by stronger industry returns than usual (from a small number of separate episodes).
